utterance: Good morning Mark, I'm one of the doctors here. I understand you've been dealing with a cough and fever for a few days. Can you tell me more about how it started and how it's been affecting you?
reply: It started three days ago with a dry, hacking cough. I've been burning up, on and off — didn't have a thermometer, but I was roasting. Since yesterday I've been bringing stuff up, it's a rusty, brownish colour at first, then clear. There's a sharp pain on the right side, round towards my back, catches me when I cough or take a deep breath.

awards.label: Chest pain with breathing or coughing

utterance: I'm sorry you've been feeling so unwell. You mentioned a sharp pain on your right side that catches when you cough or breathe deeply, and bringing up rust-coloured phlegm. These are things I want to get to the bottom of. Let me ask a few more questions. Have you measured any temperature at all, and have you had any shakes or chills?
reply: I didn't measure any temperature, but the first night I was shaking under the doona, teeth chattering, even though I was boiling. I had some shakes and chills, yeah.

utterance: Are you feeling short of breath at all — at rest or when you move around?
reply: I'm only going up the stairs. I got puffed on the way in from the car park. Sitting here I'm alright.

utterance: Have you coughed up any actual blood, or noticed wheezing or a tight chest?
reply: No actual blood, just that rusty colour. I haven't noticed any wheezing or tight chest, and I've never had asthma or anything like that.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Coughing up blood

utterance: Are you bringing up much phlegm each time now, and have you noticed any nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, or muscle aches?
reply: No, no vomiting. I don't think I've had any nausea or diarrhoea. No headache. I've had some muscle aches, but not sure if they're from the fever or just being rotten.

utterance: Have you felt confused, drowsy, or less like yourself at any point over the last few days?
reply: No, my head's clear. My wife reckons I'm just grumpy.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Confusion or drowsiness

utterance: Do you smoke, vape, or drink much alcohol? And do you have any long-term medical conditions, or take any regular medicines?
reply: No, I've never smoked, and I had a couple of beers on the weekend, none this week. No long-term medical conditions, and I take some regular blood pressure tablets.

utterance: Thanks, that's helpful. Do you remember the name of the blood pressure tablet? And have you needed any vaccines or had contact with anyone who's been unwell recently — flu, COVID, or a bad cough?
reply: I think it's Amlodipine. Didn't get round to the flu jab this year. No, I haven't had contact with anyone who's been unwell recently.

utterance: Had anything like this before — any past chest infections or pneumonia? And have you travelled anywhere recently, or been around birds, farm animals, or anyone with tuberculosis?
reply: No, I haven't had anything like this before — no chest infections or pneumonia. I haven't travelled anywhere recently, just school and home. We've got a dog, but no birds. I've not been around anyone with tuberculosis.

utterance: Just a couple more things. Have you noticed any recent weight loss, night sweats (separate from this current illness), or a change in your appetite? And is there any swelling or pain in just one leg that you've noticed?
reply: If anything I could lose a few kilos, but not sure if that's from being rotten or just me. Legs are fine, no swelling or pain in either one.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Leg swelling or calf pain

utterance:
Mark, I've examined you and done a chest X-ray, and the picture is quite clear: you have a pneumonia — an infection in the lower part of your right lung. That explains the fever, the coughing up rust-coloured phlegm, and the sharp pain when you breathe or cough.

The good news is it's not severe enough to need hospital. I'm starting you on an antibiotic called amoxicillin, 1 gram three times a day for five days. Please take all of them even if you start feeling better.

For the fever and aches, you can take paracetamol as directed on the packet, and keep your fluids up.
reply: I'm not sure how I got it, but I guess I'll take the antibiotics. I didn't have any antibiotics before, so that's probably why it's not clearing up. I'll make sure to take all five days of them, even if I start feeling better.

utterance:
That's right — most coughs are viral and settle on their own, which is why antibiotics aren't usually needed, but pneumonia is a bacterial lung infection that does need them, so this is the right time for antibiotics.

A few more things I want you to know. I'm checking your blood tests and a virus swab, and I'll review the results tomorrow. I'd like you to come back to see me — or be in touch — in about two days so I can make sure you're improving, and if your bloods show anything that needs changing I'll let you know.

Most importantly, please come back or go to the nearest emergency department straight away if you get worse: if you become very short of breath at rest, if your lips or face look blue, if you become confused or very drowsy, if you cough up fresh blood, if you can't keep fluids down, or if the fever doesn't start settling within a couple of days.

Do you have any questions for me?
reply: No questions, just thanks. I'll take the antibiotics and come back in two days. If I get worse, I'll go to the ED.
